scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You are in a first job interview on Friday with the person hiring for the role. The main worry is questions about your past experience, so this scene focuses on presenting previous work clearly and understanding what the job usually involves.
Learner: Candidate. Partner: Interviewer.
Not in this scene: talking about your strengths and weaknesses, salary, next steps after the interview.
scenes.image_prompt: realistic photo of a candidate sitting across from an interviewer in an office, notebooks on the desk, natural light, no text, no logos, no faces in close-up

must_say: say why you want this job — slot: the reason
say what you do well at work — slot: the skill
answer whether you can do a task — slot: the task
answer whether you can start on a date — slot: the date
ask whether training is provided — slot: none
ask what the next step is — slot: none
confirm you are interested in the job — slot: the position
must_understand: asks why you want this job
asks what you are good at and whether you can do a task
tells you the next step after the interview
scenes.topic_description:
Situation: After discussing your background, the interviewer moves to the key decision points of the interview. This is where they judge your fit for the role, your practical ability, and your availability, and where you need to understand what happens after the meeting.
Learner: Candidate. Partner: Interviewer.
Not in this scene: giving your name, naming the position, describing previous workplaces and duties, discussing salary.
scenes.image_prompt: realistic photo of the later stage of a job interview in an office, interviewer listening and candidate speaking, papers on desk, no text, no logos, no faces in close-up
